questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painless, indurated ulcer on the glans penis for 2 weeks. The base is clean and the edges are raised. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged but non-tender. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (Treponema pallidum) classically presents as a single, painless, indurated ulcer (chancre) with clean base and raised edges. Non-tender regional lymphadenopathy is characteristic. Chancroid is painful; herpes causes multiple painful vesicles/ulcers.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman develops tense fluid-filled blisters on normal-appearing and erythematous skin, predominantly over the flexural areas. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense blisters on normal or erythematous skin, spares mucosae, Nikolsky sign negative. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ (hemidesmosomes). Pemphigus shows flaccid blisters, positive Nikolsky, intra-epidermal split, and IgG at keratinocyte surfaces.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child presents with erythematous, scaly, non-tender plaques on the scalp with broken-off hairs. Microscopy of the hair shows arthroconidia outside the hair shaft (ectothrix). The causative organism is most likely:
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes ectothrix tinea capitis — spores are arranged in a sheath outside the hair shaft. Trichophyton tonsurans and T. violaceum cause endothrix infection (spores inside hair shaft). Epidermophyton floccosum does not infect hair.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on WHO-MDT regimen develops sudden high fever, acute neuritis, and new skin lesions that become erythematous and tender. The patient also has lymphadenopathy and joint pains. The most appropriate immediate management is:
questions.exp: This presentation is Type 1 lepra reaction (reversal reaction) — characterized by acute inflammation of pre-existing lesions, neuritis, and fever. Treatment is prednisolone (systemic corticosteroids) to prevent nerve damage. Thalidomide is used for Type 2 (ENL) reaction in males.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with butterfly-shaped erythema across the cheeks and nose, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, and joint pain for 3 months. ANA is positive at 1:640 with homogeneous pattern. The most specific autoantibody for her likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Anti-Sm (anti-Smith) is the most specific antibody for SLE (specificity ~99%), though less sensitive (~25%). Anti-dsDNA is also specific for SLE and correlates with disease activity and nephritis. Anti-Ro is associated with neonatal lupus and Sjogren's. Anti-Jo-1 is seen in dermatomyositis/polymyositis.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man presents with well-demarcated, erythematous plaques covered with silvery-white scales on elbows and knees. He also complains of nail pitting. Auspitz sign is positive. The characteristic histopathological finding is:
questions.exp: Psoriasis histology shows parakeratosis, elongated rete ridges, thinned suprapapillary epidermis, and Munro's microabscesses (neutrophils in stratum corneum). Pautrier's microabscesses are seen in mycosis fungoides. Acantholysis is seen in pemphigus. Civatte bodies are seen in lichen planus.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with clustered vesicles on an erythematous base in the L2 dermatome on the left side, with severe burning pain preceding the rash by 3 days. The treatment of choice to reduce post-herpetic neuralgia is:
opts: Oral acyclovir 800 mg 5 times/day for 7 days
questions.exp: Herpes zoster requires oral acyclovir 800 mg 5 times/day for 7 days (or valacyclovir 1g TID) to reduce severity and duration. Starting within 72 hours reduces risk of post-herpetic neuralgia. The 200 mg dose is used for herpes simplex. IV foscarnet is for acyclovir-resistant cases.

questions.q: A 25-year-old patient with leprosy has a bacterial index (BI) of 3+ on slit-skin smear. According to WHO classification, this patient should receive:
questions.exp: Patients with positive slit-skin smear (BI >0) are classified as multibacillary (MB) leprosy and receive MB-MDT for 12 months (rifampicin 600 mg monthly supervised + clofazimine 300 mg monthly + dapsone 100 mg daily + clofazimine 50 mg daily).

questions.q: A 40-year-old HIV-positive man presents with multiple hyperpigmented, non-pruritic nodules on the trunk, lower extremities, and oral mucosa. Biopsy shows spindle cells forming vascular slits with extravasated red blood cells. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Kaposi sarcoma in HIV patients (epidemic KS) presents as violaceous/hyperpigmented nodules on skin and mucosae. Histology shows spindle cells, vascular slits, and extravasated RBCs. HHV-8 (KSHV) is the causative agent. Bacillary angiomatosis (Bartonella) mimics KS but shows neutrophilic infiltrate and bacteria.

questions.q: A 35-year-old woman presents with diffuse non-scarring alopecia with positive hair pull test (telogen effluvium pattern). She reports significant weight loss and fatigue. The most important investigation to order first is:
questions.exp: Thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism most commonly) is a classic systemic cause of telogen effluvium. TSH is the most important first-line test. Hypothyroidism causes diffuse hair loss, fatigue, and weight gain; hyperthyroidism also causes hair loss. Other causes include iron deficiency, post-partum state, and stress.

questions.q: A patient presents with itchy, hypopigmented anaesthetic patches with thickened peripheral nerves. Slit-skin smear is negative. The lepromin test is strongly positive. This patient has:
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) has few (1-5), well-defined hypopigmented anaesthetic patches, thickened peripheral nerve, negative SSS, and strongly positive lepromin (Mitsuda) test — indicating good cellular immunity. LL has numerous lesions, positive SSS, and negative lepromin test.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man with a history of chronic sun exposure presents with a pearly, translucent nodule with telangiectasias and a rolled border on the nose. The most likely diagnosis and recommended treatment are:
opts: Basal cell carcinoma; Mohs micrographic surgery
Merkel cell carcinoma; wide local excision
questions.exp: Nodular BCC presents as a pearly translucent nodule with telangiectasias and rolled borders, typically on sun-exposed skin of the nose. Mohs micrographic surgery offers the highest cure rate for BCC on the face (H-zone). It allows complete margin assessment while sparing maximal tissue.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman on oral contraceptives presents with irregular, brownish hyperpigmentation on the upper lip, cheeks, and forehead, worsening in summer. The most appropriate first-line treatment is:
questions.exp: Melasma first-line treatment is the triple combination cream (Kligman's modified formula) containing hydroquinone 4% + tretinoin 0.05% + fluocinolone acetonide 0.01%, which is more effective than any single agent. Strict photoprotection is mandatory. OCP should be discontinued if possible.

questions.q: A 20-year-old presents with grouped pruritic papulovesicles over the elbows, knees, and buttocks. Skin biopsy shows subepidermal blister with neutrophils in papillary dermal tips. DIF shows granular IgA deposits in the dermal papillae. The underlying association is:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (Duhring's disease) is pathognomonic of celiac disease. DIF shows granular IgA at dermal papillae. Dapsone provides rapid relief of pruritus. Gluten-free diet leads to resolution of both skin and bowel disease. Anti-endomysial and anti-tTG antibodies are positive.

questions.q: A 50-year-old man presents with annular, scaly plaques on the trunk with central clearing. KOH examination shows septate hyphae and arthroconidia. The treatment of choice for extensive disease is:
questions.exp: Terbinafine (oral) is the treatment of choice for extensive tinea corporis and tinea cruris — it is fungicidal, acts by inhibiting squalene epoxidase, and requires shorter treatment duration compared to griseofulvin. Griseofulvin is fungistatic. Topical agents are used for limited disease.

questions.q: A neonate develops vesicles and erosions in the oral mucosa and scalp within 48 hours of birth. The mother had a history of genital herpes. The most serious complication that must be immediately addressed is:
questions.exp: Neonatal herpes (HSV-2 usually, acquired during delivery) can cause disseminated disease with CNS involvement (encephalitis) — high mortality if untreated. IV acyclovir must be started immediately. CNS involvement is diagnosed by PCR of CSF. Neonatal HSV is an emergency requiring immediate antiviral treatment.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules over the knuckles, and periungual telangiectasias. CPK is markedly elevated. The most important investigation to guide prognosis is:
opts: CT chest/abdomen/pelvis to screen for malignancy
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis in adults >40 years has a 20-30% association with underlying malignancy (lung, ovarian, gastric, colorectal, breast, lymphoma). Malignancy workup (CT CAP, mammogram, PET-CT) is mandatory and guides prognosis. Muscle biopsy confirms diagnosis but doesn't guide prognosis as well.

questions.q: A 35-year-old sexually active man presents with painful genital ulcers, and a fluctuant unilateral inguinal lymph node (bubo). Gram stain of the ulcer exudate shows 'school of fish' pattern. The causative organism is:
questions.exp: Chancroid (Haemophilus ducreyi) causes painful genital ulcers with soft necrotic base and tender inguinal buboes. The 'school of fish' or 'railroad track' pattern on Gram stain is characteristic of H. ducreyi. Treatment is azithromycin 1g single dose or ceftriaxone 250 mg IM.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with erythema, scaling, and fissuring of the palms and soles, with subungual hyperkeratosis. He has a history of similar problems in the groin. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: The 'two feet-one hand' syndrome is classic for tinea manuum + tinea pedis — one or both hands are involved with both feet affected. The history of tinea cruris supports a dermatophyte cause. KOH examination confirms the diagnosis. Treatment is oral terbinafine or itraconazole.

questions.q: A patient on long-term methotrexate for psoriasis develops nausea, oral ulcers, and macrocytic anemia. The mechanism of toxicity and the antidote are:
questions.exp: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase causing functional folate deficiency. For acute toxicity (mucositis, myelosuppression), leucovorin (folinic acid) bypasses the blocked enzyme. For chronic prophylaxis, folic acid supplementation reduces side effects without reducing efficacy. Folinic acid is the antidote in acute toxicity.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman presents with palpable purpura on the lower limbs. Skin biopsy shows leukocytoclastic vasculitis with IgA deposition on DIF. She also has arthralgia, abdominal pain, and haematuria. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Henoch-Schönlein Purpura (HSP/IgA vasculitis) is characterized by the tetrad: palpable purpura (lower limbs), arthralgia, abdominal pain, and renal involvement. DIF shows IgA deposits in vessel walls. It is the most common vasculitis in children but also occurs in adults.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with multiple comedones, inflamed papules, pustules, and nodules on the face, back, and chest. He has tried topical benzoyl peroxide without adequate response. The most appropriate next step is:
opts: Oral doxycycline + topical adapalene + topical benzoyl peroxide
questions.exp: Moderate-to-severe inflammatory acne with inadequate topical response requires combination oral antibiotic (doxycycline/tetracycline) + topical retinoid (adapalene) + topical benzoyl peroxide (to limit antibiotic resistance). Isotretinoin is reserved for severe nodulo-cystic acne or refractory cases.

questions.q: A 70-year-old man presents with a verrucous plaque with irregular borders on the lower lip that has grown over 6 months. The plaque bleeds on minor trauma. Biopsy shows atypical keratinocytes breaching the basement membrane. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) on the lip presents as an indurated, verrucous, ulcerated plaque that bleeds easily. Invasion through the basement membrane on histology confirms SCC. The lip is a high-risk site with significant metastatic potential. Treatment is wide local excision with sentinel node biopsy if indicated.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with itchy, violaceous, flat-topped polygonal papules on the flexor aspect of wrists and ankles. Wickham's striae are visible on the surface. Oral mucosa shows a lacy white pattern. The characteristic histology shows:
opts: Band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the dermo-epidermal junction with saw-tooth rete ridges
questions.exp: Lichen planus histology shows: hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, 'saw-tooth' rete ridges, band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the DEJ, and Civatte bodies (dyskeratotic keratinocytes). The 6 Ps of LP: Purple, Polygonal, Pruritic, Planar (flat-topped), Papules, Plaques.

questions.q: A patient with extensive plaque psoriasis fails to respond to methotrexate and cyclosporine. Biologics are being considered. Which biologic specifically targets IL-17A and is approved for psoriasis?
questions.exp: Secukinumab (anti-IL-17A monoclonal antibody) is highly effective for moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. It targets IL-17A specifically. Ustekinumab targets IL-12/IL-23 (p40 subunit). Adalimumab and infliximab are anti-TNF-alpha agents. IL-17 pathway is central to psoriasis pathogenesis.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman presents with recurrent aphthous ulcers, painful genital ulcers, and hypopyon uveitis. She also has pseudofolliculitis and a positive pathergy test. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Behçet's disease presents with recurrent oral aphthae, genital ulcers, ocular involvement (hypopyon uveitis — pathognomonic), and positive pathergy test. It is a systemic vasculitis common along the Silk Road (Middle East, Turkey, East Asia). Treatment includes colchicine, dapsone, and immunosuppressants.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the mouth and nostrils. The lesions began as vesicles that ruptured. The most likely causative organism and first-line oral treatment are:
opts: Staphylococcus aureus / Streptococcus pyogenes; cephalexin or dicloxacillin
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo is caused by S. aureus and/or S. pyogenes. The honey-colored crust is characteristic. First-line oral antibiotics are cephalexin or dicloxacillin (anti-staphylococcal). Topical mupirocin or retapamulin is used for localized disease. MRSA coverage is added if community MRSA is prevalent.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man presents with a painful, beefy-red, granulomatous ulcer on the glans penis with satellite lesions. No inguinal lymphadenopathy is present. Tissue smear shows Donovan bodies within large mononuclear cells. The treatment of choice is:
questions.exp: Donovanosis (Granuloma inguinale) caused by Klebsiella granulomatis presents as beefy-red granulomatous ulcers with Donovan bodies (intracellular bacteria in macrophages). Treatment of choice is doxycycline 100 mg BD for at least 3 weeks (or until lesions heal). Azithromycin is an alternative.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with skin thickening and tightening, Raynaud's phenomenon, dysphagia, and telangiectasias. She has the CREST syndrome variant. The antibody most specific to this limited form is:
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibody (ACA) is highly specific for limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (CREST syndrome: Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasias). Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I) is associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis and pulmonary fibrosis.

questions.q: A patient develops widespread blistering and erosions involving >30% BSA with mucosal involvement, following a sulfonamide drug. The Nikolsky sign is positive. The condition is:
questions.exp: Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) involves >30% BSA with epidermal detachment, positive Nikolsky sign, and mucosal involvement. Common drug triggers include sulfonamides, antiepileptics, allopurinol, NSAIDs. SCORTEN score guides prognosis. Management: ICU, stop offending drug, supportive care, IVIG or cyclosporin.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman on dapsone for leprosy develops acute onset jaundice, pallor, and fatigue. CBC shows Hb 7 g/dL with bite cells and Heinz bodies on blood smear. The diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Dapsone (and other oxidant drugs) can precipitate acute hemolytic anemia in G6PD-deficient patients. Heinz bodies (denatured hemoglobin) and bite cells on smear are characteristic. G6PD deficiency is common in India. G6PD testing should be done before starting dapsone in at-risk populations. Methemoglobinemia is another dapsone side effect.
